subject: Operational handback, runbook deposit, and limited license scope for private deployment
messages:
From: Anya Romanov <anya.romanov@helixhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Helix <procurement@helixhealth.com>, CISO Helix <ciso@helixhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on operational handback & runbook for private deployment

Hi Karthik / Marissa —

Thanks for the draft Order Form. As part of Helix's onboarding checklist for any on-prem/private deployment, our legal and security teams have a few follow-up asks related to operational handback and license boundaries before we can proceed to signature:

1) Escrow-like deposit: we ask for an assurance mechanism so our operations team can recover service if Redwood is unavailable. Helix prefers a deposit of an operational runbook and binary checksums to a neutral escrow (or equivalent).

2) Operator access & break-glass: we need explicit language limiting Redwood operator access to emergency only, with mutually-agreed windows and audit logs.

3) License scope clarity: the Order Form should explicitly state that the license for on-prem software is for Helix internal clinical use only (no sublicensing or hosting rights).

4) Audit and evidence: Helix may request a quarterly attestation and the right to perform a 1x onsite audit per 12 months with reasonable notice.

We attached a short list of suggested contract language and some background on our security requirements (Helix_Addendum_questions.docx).

Can you confirm which items Redwood will accept as written vs. proposed alternatives? We are sensitive about any broad operator or IP-handback language.

Appreciate a quick read — our procurement deadline is 11/20. Happy to jump on a call if easier.

Best,
Anya
Anya Romanov
Head of Platform Security, Helix Health
anya.romanov@helixhealth.com

Attachment: Helix_Addendum_questions.docx (document with suggested redlines)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Anya Romanov <anya.romanov@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on operational handback & runbook for private deployment

Anya —

Thanks for the clear summary and the attached doc. We appreciate Helix's security posture and can accommodate most asks with a combination of contractual commitments and operational controls. Quick summary below, then I attached our proposed redline (Redwood_proposed_redline_v1.pdf) and a draft runbook:

- Escrow-like deposit: We can't place production binaries in a third-party escrow as a standard practice. Alternative we propose: an encrypted snapshot of the deployment tooling and SHA256 checksums placed into a customer-controlled S3 bucket (customer KMS key) plus a signed attestation from Redwood. This gives Helix access to artifacts without transferring IP.

- Operator access: We accept "emergency-only, break-glass" operator access language with clear approval workflow (two-person approval from Helix security + Redwood on-call) and an automatic immutable audit trail for every operator session. We'll add precise timing and notice windows in the redline.

- License scope: Agree to tighten license language to "Internal clinical operations only — no hosting, SaaS, or sublicensing." We'll add explicit prohibitions in the Order Form exhibit A.

- Audits: We can support a 1x per year on-site audit limited to operational controls and the runbook; Redwood reserves the right to require reasonable notice (30 days) and to redact commercial pricing. Quarterly attestation (machine-generated summary logs) is doable.

Next steps: please review the attached redline, the draft runbook (PrivDeploy_Runbook_draft.docx), and tell us any language you cannot accept. If ok, suggest 30/60/90 day milestones for onboarding and post-go-live runbook handoff.

If it helps, we can put this on a 30 minute legal + security call this week.

Thanks —
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Director, Sales — Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Attachments: Redwood_proposed_redline_v1.pdf; PrivDeploy_Runbook_draft.docx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on operational handback & runbook for private deployment

Team —

Quick internal note before we finalize external reply:

- Pricing / credit: Helix asked for significant operational guarantees; we should propose a one-time onboarding credit in exchange for the runbook alternative (encrypted snapshot to customer S3). Diego — can ops estimate the engineering effort to produce the signed snapshot and a one-time assisted handoff?

- Legal redlines: Laura, please review the proposed edits to MSA Sections 4.2 (License) and 9.1 (Audit) — specifically the proposed notice period and the carve-outs for pricing.

- Rollback / kill-switch: Engineering needs to confirm whether we can provide a documented kill-switch procedure for Helix to isolate the model in a controlled fail-open vs fail-close mode; this is different from operator access. If we can do a documented mechanism, Helix may accept fewer escrow demands.

I recommend we offer the runbook snapshot + monthly attestation logs, keep escrow off the table, and be willing to accept the emergency operator access language with strict controls. We'll ask for a procurement-deal credit of 7.5% tied to a 12-month commitment.

–Marissa

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Anya Romanov <anya.romanov@helixhealth.com>, Procurement Helix <procurement@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Nov 2026 16:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions on operational handback & runbook for private deployment

Anya —

Following internal review, attached is Redwood_proposed_redline_v1.pdf with specific edits to the MSA and Order Form and a draft PrivDeploy_Runbook_draft.docx for Helix review. Summary of our final positions below (short bullets for legal/ops):

- Runbook / deposit: Redwood will provide a signed operational snapshot (deployment scripts, configuration manifests, and SHA256 checksums) and deliver those artifacts into a Helix-managed S3 bucket encrypted with Helix KMS. Redwood will not escrow source code or production binaries to a third party.

- Emergency operator access: We consent to emergency-only access with a documented break-glass workflow: Helix must approve per incident (two approvers: Helix security lead + Redwood on-call), access sessions will be recorded and retained for 12 months, and post-incident report will be provided within 5 business days.

- License scope: Order Form Exhibit A updated to restrict use to Helix internal clinical operations; no hosting, commercialization, or sublicensing allowed.

- Audit/attestation: Helix may perform one on-site audit per 12 months focused only on operational controls and runbook adherence; Redwood requires 30 days' notice and may redact pricing and unrelated commercial data. Redwood will also provide automated monthly attestation logs (a summary of control checks).

- Commercial concession: Redwood is willing to provide a one-time onboarding credit of 7% of the first year committed spend contingent on a 12-month minimum term.

Requested actions from Helix: please confirm which items above are acceptable or highlight the exact language you need changed. If acceptable, propose two available 30-minute slots next week for a legal + security alignment call, and we will work to finalize redlines by 11/20 to meet your procurement cadence.

Thanks,
Karthik

Attachments: Redwood_proposed_redline_v1.pdf; PrivDeploy_Runbook_draft.docx
